definition: A common first interview question about your background.
exampleSentence: Most interviews start with the question "Tell me about yourself."

definition: Your best qualities and the areas you need to improve.
exampleSentence: Prepare honest examples of your strengths and weaknesses before the interview.

definition: The time you must keep working after you resign.
exampleSentence: My notice period is one month, so I can start in March.

definition: The amount of money you hope to earn in a new job.
exampleSentence: The recruiter asked about my salary expectations in the first call.

term: why do you want to work here
definition: A question about your reasons for choosing the company.
exampleSentence: Research the company so you can answer "Why do you want to work here?"

term: where do you see yourself in five years
turkish: beş yıl sonra kendinizi nerede görüyorsunuz
definition: A question about your long-term career plans.
exampleSentence: A common interview question is "Where do you see yourself in five years?"

definition: Asks you to explain your past jobs in order.
exampleSentence: The manager said, "Walk me through your resume, starting with your first job."

definition: A letter sent with your CV that explains why you want the job.
exampleSentence: Write a short cover letter for each job you apply for.

definition: The manager who decides whether to hire you.
exampleSentence: The second interview was with the hiring manager and two engineers.

definition: A person who finds candidates for jobs.
exampleSentence: A recruiter contacted me on LinkedIn about a backend role.

definition: An official offer of a position from a company.
exampleSentence: She received a job offer from a bank in Istanbul.

definition: A better offer made in response to another offer.
exampleSentence: When I resigned, my company made a counteroffer with a higher salary.

definition: The first months of a job when the company checks your work.
exampleSentence: The probation period at our company lasts three months.

definition: The day you begin a new job.
exampleSentence: We agreed on a start date at the beginning of next month.

definition: Working the normal number of hours each week.
exampleSentence: This is a full-time position with flexible working hours.

definition: Working fewer hours than a normal working week.
exampleSentence: Many students look for part-time jobs during university.

definition: Moving to another city or country for a job.
exampleSentence: The company offers help with relocation to Berlin.

definition: Extra things you get with a job, such as insurance and bonuses.
exampleSentence: The benefits package includes private health insurance and a gym membership.

definition: What you want to achieve in your working life.
exampleSentence: My career goals include leading a small development team.

definition: Personal skills such as communication and teamwork.
exampleSentence: Employers value soft skills as much as technical knowledge.

definition: Skills you can measure, such as coding or languages.
exampleSentence: Python and SQL are the hard skills listed in the job description.

definition: An interview that tests your technical knowledge.
exampleSentence: I practiced coding problems every day before the technical interview.

definition: A programming task given during the hiring process.
exampleSentence: The first step is an online coding challenge that takes one hour.

definition: A task you complete at home and send to the company.
exampleSentence: The take-home assignment was to build a small web app.

definition: An interview where you solve problems on a whiteboard.
exampleSentence: In my whiteboard interview, I had to draw the database design.

definition: An interview where you design a large software system.
exampleSentence: In the system design interview, they asked me to design a chat app.

definition: A question about how you acted in a real situation.
exampleSentence: A typical behavioral question is about a conflict with a colleague.

definition: A way to answer interview questions: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
exampleSentence: Use the STAR method to give clear answers with real examples.

definition: A collection of your best work to show employers.
exampleSentence: Share a link to your portfolio with your best projects.

definition: A check of your past jobs, education or records before hiring.
exampleSentence: The company runs a background check before sending the contract.

definition: A small list of the best candidates chosen for the next step.
exampleSentence: I was happy to hear that I was on the shortlist for the role.

definition: An interview at the company's office.
exampleSentence: After two online calls, they invited me to an onsite interview.

definition: An email sent after an interview to thank the interviewers.
exampleSentence: Send a short follow-up email within one day of the interview.

definition: A polite thanks at the end of an interview.
exampleSentence: At the end, I said, "Thank you for your time and the interesting chat."

term: do you have any questions for us
turkish: bize sormak istediğiniz bir şey var mı
definition: Asked at the end of an interview so you can ask questions.
exampleSentence: Always prepare an answer for "Do you have any questions for us?"

definition: Says that you learn new things fast.
exampleSentence: I told them that I'm a quick learner and enjoy new tools.

definition: Says that you stay calm and productive when work is stressful.
exampleSentence: Give an example when you say I work well under pressure.

definition: Introduces the success you are most proud of.
exampleSentence: My biggest achievement was reducing the app's loading time by half.

definition: Why you want to leave or left your last job.
exampleSentence: Keep your reason for leaving positive and short.

definition: The company you worked for before.
exampleSentence: Never criticize your previous employer during a job interview.
